risk.rationale: The only verified finding is F1 (LIKELY 0.6): a sign-in from a previously unseen device PH-9900 versus the usual device LT-6002 for b.cetin@aegean.edu (T1078). This is a single weak, unexplained signal — not a confirmed account takeover chain (no MFA bypass, no post-compromise activity, no confirmed malicious action), so contain is not met. It is also not explained away (no legitimate basis given for PH-9900), so benign is not met. The two password-spray claims were rejected: both source IPs are shared egress (186 and 208 distinct MFA accounts in 30 days, above the 10 threshold), with failures spread across many accounts consistent with background noise. No data-quality conflicts exist. With no exposure and no conflicting/insufficient evidence requiring human review, escalate is not met. This fits monitor: a weak unexplained signal to watch. Per gate policy, no dissent from the obvious call is made, and no CONFIRMED finding is needed to override.
